# spry-turn

> Lightweight Rust STUN/TURN server, embeddable native relay and WASM packet codec. MIT; maintained by TheCryptoDonkey under ForgeSworn.

Version 0.1.0. Repository and initial GitHub prerelease are private; authorised access is required for source and release artefacts. There is no crates.io, docs.rs or npm publication, hosted relay, credential service or public documentation site.

Native UDP/TCP clients and optional TLS use UDP peer allocations. Browser applications use their existing WebRTC ICE implementation. Ordinary browser WASM cannot host a raw-socket TURN server. Shared TURN secrets belong only to trusted operator tools; give clients short-lived credentials.

This is an initial implementation, without full coturn parity or production qualification. UDP peer-relay port ranges are optional and fail closed on exhaustion. Static user databases, TCP relay allocations, DTLS, dual allocations and deployed Archy/Sapflow integration are not implemented. Physical phone and public-network acceptance remain open.

Native ARM64 M4 Max UDP loopback measurements show 17–22% more throughput than the tested coturn configuration. The connected-UDP optimisation adds one socket per allocation, and process RSS excludes kernel buffers. Consult the benchmark method before reusing any figures.

These files provide navigation and source context for authorised readers and tools. They do not change repository visibility or guarantee indexing by search engines or language models.

Generated by scripts/docs.mjs; edit source guides and run npm run docs:generate.

---

## Source: Overview

Canonical source: [README.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/README.md)

# spry-turn

A lightweight standalone **STUN/TURN server in Rust**, an embeddable native
library and a portable **WebAssembly packet codec**. UDP and TCP clients,
optional TLS, coturn-compatible shared-secret credentials, bounded resources
and no media stack. MIT licensed; the repository and initial release are private.

[Documentation](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/README.md) · [Quick start](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md) ·
[WebRTC and native integration](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/integration.md) ·
[Coturn compatibility](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/coturn-compatibility.md) ·
[API](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/api.md) · [Support development](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/SUPPORT.md#donations) ·
[LLM index](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/llms.txt)

In the measured native Apple M4 Max UDP loopback comparison, spry-turn
delivered **17–22% more packets/s** than the tested coturn configuration,
with **19–23% less server CPU time** and **78–82% less process RSS**.
The optimisation uses an extra UDP socket per allocation; RSS excludes
kernel socket buffers. These results do not establish WAN, Linux or TLS
performance. See [the method, raw results and limitations](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md).

The first target is a server running independently on a normal computer.
Later, an Archy owner can install it and configure KithMoot to use their
chosen TURN address and credentials. The software publisher operates no
relay, credential service, discovery directory or calling entitlement.
There are no hosted defaults in the code.

## What works

- STUN Binding, authenticated TURN Allocate and Refresh, CreatePermission,
  ChannelBind, Send/Data indications and ChannelData.
- UDP relaying, with clients connecting over UDP or TCP. The `tls` feature
  adds TLS 1.2/1.3 client connections using rustls.
- Coturn-compatible TURN REST credentials: expiry-prefixed usernames and
  a shared secret. Credential generation is an operator-run local command.
- IPv4 or IPv6 relay address family per configured instance. Native IPv6
  sockets and XOR address encoding are supported; dual allocations are not.
- Expiring allocations, IP permissions and channel bindings; bounded
  allocations, per-user allocations, connections, peers, stream buffers,
  control request rate and per-allocation bandwidth.
- Private, loopback, link-local and multicast targets blocked by default.
  Explicit loopback testing is restricted to a loopback-only listener.
- No media decoders, WebRTC stack, database, async runtime, admin website,
  analytics, access log, room membership or application admission service.

The UDP ChannelData path borrows incoming payloads and reserves header space
in its receive buffer, avoiding a payload copy on the return path. One
non-blocking Mio event loop owns sockets and allocation state; no per-packet
tasks or worker queues. Generation-tagged slots route readiness events
without hashing internal tokens and reject stale events after reuse.
TCP/TLS uses bounded output buffers.
The library forbids unsafe Rust in its own code; dependencies may use it.

Concrete IPv4 listeners use a connected client-facing UDP socket per
allocation to retain the client's fixed five-tuple in the kernel. This
improves the measured send/receive path and costs one additional UDP socket
per client. Wildcard/IPv6 listeners and unavailable fast-path sockets retain
standard forwarding. The portable build is available with
`--no-default-features --features runtime,turn`. RSS measurements exclude
kernel socket memory; see the comparison's socket counts and limitations.

This is an initial implementation, not full coturn parity or a production
qualification. [Compatibility and remaining work](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/GOALS.md) are explicit.

## Run locally

Rust 1.85 or later; stable Rust 1.94 is tested. Build output uses `target/`.

```sh
cargo build --release
export SPRY_TURN_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
./target/release/spry-turn serve
```

The default UDP/TCP listener is `127.0.0.1:3478`. Generate a short-lived
credential locally using the same environment:

```sh
./target/release/spry-turn credential --ttl 3600 --label client
```

For larger workloads, size the process file-descriptor limit for listeners,
two sockets per optimised UDP allocation and any TCP/TLS connections.
`--max-allocations` limits logical allocations; it cannot raise an OS limit.
The comparison runner sets 4,096 for its own processes only.

Use an opaque transport label. Do not put room IDs, personal identities or
application membership in usernames. The credential output is a secret;
do not commit it or put it in public logs. The shared secret never belongs
in a browser, join URL or client build. Operators decide how to give their
own users credentials; no remotely callable credential issuer is included.

Configure a standard ICE client with `turn:HOST:3478?transport=udp` or
`turn:HOST:3478?transport=tcp`, the generated username and credential. A
website uses its browser's existing WebRTC support; it does not host TURN.

To listen on a chosen interface, supply `--listen IP:PORT` and, if needed,
`--relay-ip IP`. Wildcard listeners require an explicit concrete relay IP.
`--public-ip IP` advertises an operator-configured NAT address. The
operator must provide actual reachability and firewall rules; installing
the server cannot make an inaccessible home connection a public relay.

TLS is optional at build time:

```sh
cargo build --release --features tls
./target/release/spry-turn serve --tls-listen 127.0.0.1:5349 \
  --tls-cert certificate.pem --tls-key private-key.pem
```

Use a certificate trusted by the intended clients. Local tests generate
temporary certificates and test trust separately from public deployment.
The process has no certificate renewal or TLS file watcher yet.

## Embed

`spry_turn::turn::Server::bind(Config)` creates a server;
`poll_once(Duration)` advances its event loop. The host controls its lifetime
and configuration. No threads are started by the library. Build with
`--no-default-features --features turn` for the borrowed wire codec and
credential helpers without the socket runtime. Swift/Kotlin bindings and
physical phone acceptance are later work.

## WebAssembly

The portable packet codec and credential helpers also build to WASM,
without Mio, socket2, TLS or an OS random-number dependency:

```sh
cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown \
  --no-default-features --features wasm --lib
wasm-bindgen --target web --out-dir .local/wasm --out-name spry_turn \
  target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/spry_turn.wasm
node tests/wasm.mjs
```

Use wasm-bindgen CLI 0.2.129 to match the pinned bindings. `PacketArena`
provides a reusable region of linear memory that a host accesses through
`Uint8Array`. Channel framing/parsing reuses that region without per-packet
Rust allocations or whole-payload binding marshalling. Recreate the view
after memory growth and do not retain it after freeing the arena.

The initial module is about 56 kB. A real WASM execution test validates the
published STUN integrity vector and repeats a million framing/parsing
operations without growing linear memory. That is a protocol microbenchmark,
separate from server network throughput. Networking and allocation/session
I/O belong to the native server adapter; ordinary browser WASM cannot host
a standard raw-socket TURN server.

TURN forwards arbitrary datagrams; it has no WebRTC media semantics. A
future SRT/Sapflow client could use an appropriate transport adapter.
Unmodified SRT/RTMP applications do not automatically speak TURN. Sapflow
integration and transparent UDP forwarding are not implemented here.

## Verify

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --all-features
cargo test --no-default-features --lib
cargo test --no-default-features --features turn --lib
cargo build --release --features tls
python3 tests/interop.py --tls
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npx playwright install chromium
python3 tests/browser.py --tls
```

The independent Python stdlib client checks real UDP/TCP/TLS sockets.
Chromium forces relay/relay candidates and verifies generated video decoded,
audio received and application data returned in both directions for all
three client transports. Browser tests use a generated test certificate and
explicit browser certificate bypass; the Python TLS test validates its
generated CA. This is not public-certificate or real-phone acceptance.

The [comparison runner](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/scripts/compare.py) uses the same socket-level load
generator against each server, alternating order. It reports delivered
packets, loss/corruption, round-trip latency, RSS and server CPU. All test
servers bind loopback and clean up their processes and generated secrets.

## Scope and legal position

The chosen role is publishing software, with independent owners operating
their own relay instances. The [transport position](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/legal/transport-position.md)
records that architecture and the unresolved legal interpretations. A
private repository, MIT licence, encryption or use of TURN does not by
itself determine a future operator's Online Safety Act position.

MIT applies to our code. Dependency notices are in
[THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt); published RFC test data
is credited in [NOTICE](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/NOTICE). There is no package publication or hosted
service deployment in this repository.

# spry-turn documentation

spry-turn is a standalone Rust STUN/TURN server, an embeddable native relay
and a WASM packet codec. It is an initial implementation with measured
performance and explicit compatibility gaps. The repository and initial
GitHub release are private; there is no publisher-operated TURN service.

## Source: Getting started

Canonical source: [docs/getting-started.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md)

# Getting started

This guide runs a local standalone server. It does not expose a public
relay or require a hosted service. See [operations](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/operations.md) before
configuring an independently operated instance.

## Obtain the source

The repository is private. Use an authorised GitHub account and SSH key:

```sh
git clone git@github.com:forgesworn/spry-turn.git
cd spry-turn
```

Source is the portable installation path. Cargo and npm publication are
disabled. The private v0.1.0 GitHub prerelease also carries a macOS ARM64
TLS-enabled executable archive and a WASM codec archive. It does not make
the source or artefacts publicly downloadable. Authorised users can fetch
and verify the archives in an empty directory:

```sh
gh release download v0.1.0 --repo forgesworn/spry-turn
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
```

The macOS executable is not a Linux, Windows or phone build. A release
does not establish production or physical-device acceptance. The source
build below remains available for other supported native environments.

Rust 1.85 or newer is declared; Rust 1.94.1 and 1.96 were used for the
initial verification and native M4 measurements. Current CI checks stable
Rust on Linux and macOS. Python 3, Node 24, OpenSSL and Chromium are test
tools, not server runtime dependencies.

## Build and start

```sh
cargo build --locked --release
export SPRY_TURN_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
./target/release/spry-turn serve
```

The process binds UDP and TCP at `127.0.0.1:3478`. Keep this terminal running;
stop it with Ctrl-C. The secret must contain at least 32 bytes. This example
generates a fresh one; a real operator must store and supply their chosen
secret consistently across restarts and credential generation.

The server blocks loopback peers by default, even when its listener is
local. The following explicit local-test mode allows two local ICE clients
to send traffic through it:

```sh
./target/release/spry-turn serve --allow-loopback-peers
```

Stop the first server before starting the second command on the same port.
Loopback-peer testing is restricted to a loopback-only listener and is
unnecessary for normal public-address peers.

## Generate client credentials

Use the same secret in a separate shell or generate the credential before
starting the server:

```sh
./target/release/spry-turn credential --ttl 3600 --label client
```

The command emits JSON with `username` and `credential`. TTL is 1–86,400
seconds. Labels are 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, hyphens or underscores.
Use an opaque transport label rather than a room name or identity.

Give the client that short-lived pair through an operator-controlled
channel. The client must never receive `SPRY_TURN_SECRET`. Credential output
is sensitive; do not paste it into an issue, log or committed fixture.
See [integration](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/integration.md) for ICE configuration.

## Optional TLS

```sh
cargo build --locked --release --features tls
./target/release/spry-turn serve --tls-listen 127.0.0.1:5349 \
  --tls-cert certificate.pem --tls-key private-key.pem
```

Provide your own PEM files and client-trusted certificate. The TLS listener
is additional to the UDP/TCP listener. This initial server does not renew
certificates or reload TLS files automatically.

## Check the installation

```sh
./target/release/spry-turn --version
./target/release/spry-turn --help
python3 tests/interop.py --tls
```

The socket suite starts its own loopback server instances, generated secret
and temporary TLS fixtures, then removes them. Build with `--features tls`
before using `--tls`. Browser and WASM validation commands are in
[contributing](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

If allocation succeeds but media does not arrive, check peer policy, UDP
relay reachability and credentials before changing client transports.
The [operations guide](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/operations.md) explains the current firewall and
relay-port limitations.

## Source: Client and host integration

Canonical source: [docs/integration.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/integration.md)

# Client and host integration

TURN is an optional transport choice in the calling application. The
application or independent operator selects the server and supplies a
short-lived credential pair. spry-turn supplies neither room admission
nor a hosted credential endpoint.

## Browser WebRTC

Use the browser's existing ICE implementation. This example takes a
credential pair already supplied by the selected operator:

```js
function relayConnection({ username, credential }) {
  return new RTCPeerConnection({
    iceServers: [{
      urls: [
        'turn:relay.example:3478?transport=udp',
        'turn:relay.example:3478?transport=tcp',
        'turns:relay.example:5349?transport=tcp',
      ],
      username,
      credential,
    }],
    iceTransportPolicy: 'relay',
  });
}
```

`relay.example` is a placeholder, not an included service. Only list
transports the operator has enabled and made reachable. `relay` forces
TURN for qualification; choose `all` if the application should also try
direct ICE paths. Media tracks, data channels, SDP exchange, consent,
end-to-end encryption and reconnect policy stay with the application.

The `transport=tcp` URLs describe client-to-server transport. The current
server still uses UDP allocations towards the peer. This is different
from TCP relay allocations under RFC 6062, which are not implemented.

The shared server secret must never be bundled into JavaScript, WASM, a
mobile app, a join URL or a browser storage entry. The WASM credential
helper is for trusted operator tools; it does not make exposing the secret
to clients safe.

## Native TURN clients

Existing native WebRTC clients can use the same ICE URLs, username and
password through their platform's ICE configuration. They do not need to
embed this library to use the server. Physical iOS, Android and no-Play
GrapheneOS acceptance against this implementation remain unverified.

## Embed the native Rust server

Authorised source consumers can depend on this private Git repository.
Use a reviewed full commit SHA in place of `REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA`:

```toml
[dependencies]
spry-turn = { git = "ssh://git@github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn.git", rev = "REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA" }
```

The following host starts a local server and advances its event loop:

```rust
use spry_turn::turn::{Config, Server};
use std::{io, time::Duration};

fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
    let secret = std::env::var("SPRY_TURN_SECRET")
        .map_err(io::Error::other)?
        .into_bytes();
    let mut server = Server::bind(Config::local(secret))?;
    loop {
        server.poll_once(Duration::from_secs(1))?;
    }
}
```

The host owns scheduling, shutdown and credential storage. No worker
thread starts automatically. Drop the server to close its sockets. Use a
dedicated host thread if the surrounding application cannot block in
`poll_once`; Swift/Kotlin bindings are future work. Configuration fields
and feature combinations are listed in [the API reference](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/api.md).

## Browser WASM packet codec

Build the module and glue using [the API commands](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/api.md#wasm-build).
Serve these files through the embedding application's existing asset
pipeline; there is no project-operated CDN.

```js
import init, { PacketArena } from './spry_turn.js';

const wasm = await init();
const arena = new PacketArena(2048);
let bytes = new Uint8Array(wasm.memory.buffer, arena.ptr(), arena.capacity());
const payload = new TextEncoder().encode('hello');
bytes.set(payload, 4);
if (!arena.frame_channel(0x4000, payload.length)) {
  throw new Error('packet does not fit');
}
const length = payload.length + 4;
if (arena.channel_payload_len(length) !== payload.length) {
  throw new Error('invalid channel packet');
}
// Consume or send bytes.subarray(0, length) before reusing or freeing the arena.
// Recreate bytes after any WebAssembly memory growth.
arena.free();
```

Framing a packet does not create a TURN allocation or authorise channel
`0x4000`. A host adapter must implement session control and supply actual
I/O. Ordinary browser WASM cannot open the raw UDP/TCP sockets needed to
host a standard TURN server. The codec is useful for protocol adapters and
tests; it does not replace browser WebRTC.

## KithMoot, Archy and Sapflow

KithMoot may point its normal TURN client at an independently selected
instance. An Archy owner may later install and operate that server;
packaging, exposure policy and integration are not implemented here yet.
The publisher operates no default relay, directory or credential service.

Sapflow or another non-WebRTC application would need a TURN-aware transport
adapter. Standard TURN can carry arbitrary datagrams, but unmodified SRT
or RTMP clients do not become TURN clients by changing a destination URL.
No codecs, SRT, RTMP or HLS stack is included.

---

## Source: Rust and WASM API

Canonical source: [docs/api.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/api.md)

# Rust and WASM API reference

Version 0.1.0. Source is authoritative; there is no published crates.io,
docs.rs or npm package. Authorised users can generate local Rust API pages
with `cargo doc --locked --all-features --no-deps`.

## Cargo features

| Feature | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `runtime` | Native Mio sockets and OS randomness; by itself it does not enable TURN |
| `turn` | STUN/TURN wire codec, credential helpers and nonce logic |
| `direct-index` | Native runtime and TURN, with generation-tagged readiness slots |
| `connected-udp` | `direct-index` plus concrete-IPv4 connected-socket optimisation |
| `tls` | Native runtime, TURN and optional rustls TLS client listener |
| `wasm` | TURN helpers and wasm-bindgen; the exported arena is WASM-only |

Defaults are `runtime`, `turn` and `connected-udp`. Use
`--no-default-features --features runtime,turn` for the portable native
path, `--no-default-features --features turn --lib` for codec/auth only,
or `--no-default-features --features wasm --lib` for a WASM module. The
WASM build must exclude the native defaults.

## Native configuration

Source: [src/turn.rs](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/src/turn.rs).

`Config::local(secret: Vec<u8>) -> Config` sets these defaults:

| Field | Default and purpose |
|---|---|
| `listen` | `127.0.0.1:3478`, shared UDP/TCP listening address |
| `relay_ip` | `127.0.0.1`, local bind address of UDP peer sockets |
| `relay_port_range` | `None` for OS ephemeral ports, or `Some((first, last))` for an inclusive nonzero UDP relay range with no fallback |
| `advertised_ip` | `None`; optional NAT-visible relay IP of the same address family |
| `realm` | `spry-turn`, long-term authentication realm |
| `secret` | Caller supplied, at least 32 bytes |
| `allow_loopback_peers` | `false`; explicit loopback testing |
| `max_allocations` | `1024`, total logical allocation limit |
| `max_per_user` | `8`, per-username allocation limit |
| `max_connections` | `256`, TCP/TLS connections |
| `bytes_per_second` | `67108864`, aggregate byte rate per allocation across both directions |
| `tls` | `None`; with `tls`, an optional address and `Arc<rustls::ServerConfig>` |

`Server::bind(config)` validates configuration and binds listeners. Realm
must contain 1–128 bytes, relay bind IP must be concrete and numeric limits
must be positive. A configured relay range requires `1 <= first <= last`;
port exhaustion produces TURN 508 without widening the range. The CLI additionally restricts loopback-peer opt-in to a
loopback-only listener; embedding hosts must enforce the same policy.

| Method | Result |
|---|---|
| `Server::bind(config: Config)` | `io::Result<Server>` |
| `server.local_addr()` | `io::Result<SocketAddr>` |
| `server.poll_once(timeout: Duration)` | `io::Result<()>`; processes readiness and expiry work |
| `server.stats()` | Copy of `limits::Stats` aggregate counters |
| `server.allocation_count()` | Current number of allocations |
| `turn::unix_time()` | Current epoch seconds |

The library starts no threads. A host must keep polling and drop `Server`
when it wants to close listeners and allocations. `Stats` contains
`forwarded_packets`, `forwarded_bytes` and `dropped_packets`; these are
process-local counters, not a remote monitoring or billing API.

## Wire and authentication helpers

Sources: [src/wire.rs](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/src/wire.rs), [src/auth.rs](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/src/auth.rs).

- `wire::Message::parse(&[u8]) -> Option<Message<'_>>`: borrowed STUN parser,
  with `method`, `class` and transaction ID; attributes remain borrowed.
- `message.attr(type)`, `number(type)` and `address(type)`: read attributes.
- `message.verify(key) -> bool`: verify message integrity.
- `wire::Builder::new(method, class, transaction)`: construct a STUN packet;
  `attr`, `number`, `address`, then `finish(key)` produce owned bytes.
- `wire::channel(&[u8]) -> Option<(u16, &[u8])>`: borrowed ChannelData parser.
- `wire::frame_len(&[u8]) -> Option<usize>`: obtain the declared stream frame
  length, including channel padding. Fewer than four bytes return `None`;
  an invalid leading type returns `Some(0)`. The caller must wait for that
  many bytes and validate the complete packet separately.
- `auth::credential(secret, username) -> String`: TURN REST password.
- `auth::key(username, realm, password) -> [u8; 16]`: long-term integrity key.
- `auth::expires(username) -> Option<u64>`: parse the expiry prefix.
- `auth::Nonces`: issue and validate time-, IP- and realm-bound nonces;
  `new()` uses OS randomness when `runtime` is enabled.

Parsing and integrity verification do not themselves grant a peer
permission, allocate a relay or enforce the application's membership.
For normal server use, let `Server` own the TURN state machine.

## WASM build

```sh
rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
cargo build --locked --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown \
  --no-default-features --features wasm --lib
wasm-bindgen --target web --out-dir .local/wasm --out-name spry_turn \
  target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/spry_turn.wasm
node tests/wasm.mjs
```

Use wasm-bindgen CLI 0.2.129 to match the pinned crate. Install that
specific CLI version if needed; the server does not depend on the CLI at
runtime. The generated package contains `.wasm`, JavaScript and TypeScript
declarations. See [integration](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/integration.md#browser-wasm-packet-codec).

Source: [src/wasm.rs](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/src/wasm.rs).

| JavaScript API | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `new PacketArena(capacity)` | Allocate 20–65,536 bytes once |
| `arena.ptr()` / `arena.capacity()` | Location and length for a borrowed `Uint8Array` |
| `arena.valid_stun(len)` | Validate a STUN packet in the arena |
| `arena.stun_method(len)` / `stun_class(len)` | Parsed value, or `-1` |
| `arena.verify_integrity(len, key)` | Verify an in-arena STUN packet |
| `arena.frame_channel(number, payloadLen)` | Write a ChannelData header; payload starts at offset 4 |
| `arena.channel_number(len)` / `channel_payload_len(len)` | Parsed value, or `-1` |
| `arena.free()` | Release the arena; invalidate all borrowed views |
| `rest_credential(secret, username)` | Trusted operator credential helper |

Channel numbers accepted by this initial codec are `0x4000`–`0x4fff`.
The caller owns networking, channel allocation and session authorisation.
Do not retain views across WASM memory growth or past `arena.free()`.
Credential helpers are not for placing a server secret into a public client.

## Source: Coturn compatibility

Canonical source: [docs/coturn-compatibility.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/coturn-compatibility.md)

# Coturn compatibility and migration

spry-turn implements a focused subset of STUN/TURN. It has no coturn
configuration-file parser and is not a universal drop-in replacement.
The goal is a small forwarding core with measured resource costs.

## Feature map

| Coturn deployment need | spry-turn 0.1.0 |
|---|---|
| STUN Binding | Implemented |
| TURN UDP relay allocations | Implemented |
| UDP clients | Implemented and socket/browser tested |
| TCP clients | Implemented and socket/browser tested |
| TLS clients | Optional `tls` feature; socket/browser tested with generated certificates |
| Expiring shared-secret TURN REST credentials | Implemented; operator-run credential command |
| Allocate, Refresh and explicit deallocation | Implemented |
| IP permissions, ChannelBind and ChannelData | Implemented |
| Send and Data indications | Implemented |
| IPv4 or IPv6 relay sockets | One configured family per instance; IPv6 field acceptance remains open |
| Allocation, per-user, connection and bandwidth limits | Implemented; names and semantics differ from coturn |
| NAT-advertised relay IP | `--public-ip`; actual NAT mapping is operator responsibility |
| Static long-term username/password database | Not implemented |
| Fixed UDP relay-port range | `--relay-ports FIRST:LAST`; exhaustion fails with 508, no ephemeral fallback |
| Dual allocations, EVEN-PORT and reservation tokens | Not implemented |
| RFC 8489 SHA-256 authentication | Not implemented |
| TCP relay allocations (RFC 6062) | Not implemented |
| DTLS client transport | Not implemented |
| OAuth, database backends, clustering, HTTP/telnet administration | Not implemented |
| Certificate renewal or reload | Not implemented |

Unknown comprehension-required attributes receive a 420 response. See
[GOALS.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/GOALS.md) for qualification and remaining extensions.

## Configuration concepts

These are conceptual mappings, not a compatible configuration syntax:

| Coturn concept | spry-turn equivalent |
|---|---|
| `listening-ip` and `listening-port` | `--listen IP:PORT` |
| `relay-ip` | `--relay-ip IP` |
| `min-port` / `max-port` | Inclusive `--relay-ports FIRST:LAST`; no coturn configuration-file parsing |
| `external-ip` | `--public-ip IP`; no automatic mapping discovery |
| `realm` | `--realm NAME` |
| `use-auth-secret` / `static-auth-secret` | Required `SPRY_TURN_SECRET` environment variable |
| `total-quota` | `--max-allocations COUNT` |
| `user-quota` | `--max-per-user COUNT` |
| `max-bps` | `--bytes-per-second COUNT`; assess aggregate accounting and burst behaviour separately |
| TLS listener/certificate/key | `--tls-listen`, `--tls-cert`, `--tls-key` with a TLS-enabled build |

For shared-secret clients, retain the expiry-prefixed username format and
HMAC-generated password. Do not reuse application identity or room IDs as
transport labels. The realm and nonce are server-owned authentication
inputs; coturn's live sessions and nonces are not transferred.

## Assess a deployment before switching

1. List the exact transports, authentication mode, relay address family,
   firewall port range and extensions your current clients require.
2. Compare that list with the feature map. A deployment needing a missing
   feature should continue using its current server.
3. Run an independent instance and configure an explicit test client with
   separate credentials. Do not redirect active calls during evaluation.
4. Test both endpoints, forced relay, actual decoded media/data, credential
   renewal, UDP blocking, long calls, reconnects and trusted TLS certificates.
5. Size file descriptors for the additional connected-UDP socket and test
   exhaustion and peer restrictions on the intended host/network.
6. Retain the existing ICE configuration as a rollback path. Switching a
   server address does not transfer existing allocations or guarantee ICE
   restart behaviour in an application.

## Measured performance

The native ARM64 M4 Max UDP loopback matrix recorded 17–22% higher packet
throughput than the tested coturn 4.18.0 configuration. CPU and process RSS
were lower; the optimisation also used more UDP sockets. These results
apply to the recorded workload and configuration, not all coturn uses.
See [benchmarks](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md) for latency, methodology, architecture
checks, descriptor counts, raw evidence and explicitly superseded runs.

## Source: Independent operation

Canonical source: [docs/operations.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/operations.md)

# Independent operator guide

The supported first step is a local standalone server. Public deployment,
sustained hostile-network use and production replacement of coturn remain
unqualified. This guide describes current controls and limits so an owner
can evaluate an instance deliberately.

## Addresses and reachability

The default listener is loopback only. `--listen IP:PORT` chooses the UDP
and TCP listening address. Without `--relay-ip`, the CLI uses the listener
IP for peer sockets. A wildcard listener such as `0.0.0.0:3478` requires an
explicit, concrete `--relay-ip`.

`--public-ip` changes the advertised relay IP for operator-managed NAT;
it does not configure a router, discover a mapping, open firewall ports or
solve carrier-grade NAT. Its address family must match the relay family.
Use one relay family per instance; dual allocations are not implemented.

Client listener reachability alone is insufficient. `--relay-ports FIRST:LAST`
selects an inclusive UDP peer-relay range, for example `49160:49191`. Both
ports must be nonzero and the first must not exceed the last. With this
option, allocations bind only within that range. Occupied host ports are
skipped; exhaustion returns an authenticated TURN 508 response and never
falls back to an ephemeral port. Released ports can be allocated again.
The range is not reserved at startup. Allow headroom for occupied ports,
and keep other services out of the selected range. Narrow ranges limit
available allocations even when `--max-allocations` is higher.

Without the option, peer sockets retain OS-assigned ephemeral ports for
backwards compatibility. A public package must choose a bounded range
explicitly. These bounds apply to UDP peer-relay allocations, separately
from the UDP/TCP client listener, optional TLS listener and optimised
client-facing sockets. A single-port range is supported; it does not
implement EVEN-PORT or reservation tokens.

## Public endpoint deployment plan

Public operation is still unqualified. The deploying operator owns each
step below; installing software must not open or publish a service silently.

| Item | Operator configuration and readback |
|---|---|
| Client listeners | Allow inbound UDP/TCP only on the chosen `--listen` port and TCP on the chosen TLS port; use concrete bind addresses or a deliberate wildcard listener with concrete `--relay-ip` |
| Relay sockets | Choose `--relay-ports FIRST:LAST`; allow inbound peer UDP on that range at the host and provider firewall, with required outbound UDP and return traffic |
| NAT | If used, configure one-to-one address translation and preserve relay ports; `--public-ip` changes the advertised address only |
| Certificate | Supply a currently valid chain trusted by the intended clients, with the DNS name used in their `turns:` URI covered by the certificate; keep its private key on the operator node |
| Renewal | Arrange issuance, renewal and an operator-controlled restart; files are read at startup and active allocations are lost on restart |
| Readiness | Check authenticated Allocate, permitted bidirectional traffic and trusted TLS from an independent network, including a client with UDP blocked; a listening TCP socket is insufficient |
| Retention | Read back process-manager, container, host, crash-dump and hosting-provider logging; lack of a payload/access-log writer in Spry does not disable these |

TURN over TCP/TLS still uses UDP between relay and peer. Opening only a TLS
port is insufficient. Restrict unrelated inbound services and preserve the
default private-peer restrictions. This is a plan, not an applied firewall,
certificate-renewal implementation or public-network acceptance result.
Port bounds are exposure/resource controls; they do not settle who provides
an underlying communications service or establish a legal exemption.

## Credentials

Supply `SPRY_TURN_SECRET` privately through the operator's process manager
or shell. Use an unpredictable value containing at least 32 bytes. It must
be the same value used by the credential command or trusted generator.
There is no remote credential API or static user database.

Credential usernames begin with epoch expiry seconds and an opaque label;
the password uses the coturn-compatible shared-secret HMAC scheme. The CLI
accepts a TTL of 1–86,400 seconds. Keep clocks accurate. Applications must
obtain replacement credentials before expiry and implement their own
renewal/reconnect policy; extending a username does not extend an already
issued credential. In-flight credential expiry and network recovery need
qualification in the target application.

There is no rolling dual-secret mechanism. A restart loses allocation
state, and changing the secret invalidates previously issued credentials.
Plan operator-driven rotation and client recovery; never distribute the
shared secret to calling clients.

## Resource controls

| CLI option | Default | Scope |
|---|---:|---|
| `--max-allocations` | 1024 | Total logical allocations |
| `--max-per-user` | 8 | Allocations per credential username |
| `--max-connections` | 256 | Accepted TCP/TLS connections |
| `--bytes-per-second` | 67108864 | Aggregate byte rate per allocation across both directions |

The server additionally bounds peer entries, stream queues and control
request rate in code. It has no per-room or application membership policy.
The allocation limit does not reserve memory or raise the process's file
descriptor limit. Authentication and stream setup also consume resources.

On a concrete IPv4 listener the default optimisation uses one client-facing
connected UDP socket plus one peer-facing relay socket per UDP allocation.
Budget at least those descriptors, listeners, stream connections and host
headroom. Wildcard, IPv6 and unavailable optimisation sockets use the
portable path. To select that path explicitly:

```sh
cargo build --locked --release --no-default-features --features runtime,turn
```

Process RSS omits kernel socket buffers. Use host-level measurements before
drawing total-memory or maximum-capacity conclusions. The benchmark
runner's descriptor limit applies only to its own child processes.

## Peer policy and TLS

Private, loopback, link-local and multicast peers are blocked by default.
The CLI's `--allow-loopback-peers` exists for generated local tests and
requires a loopback-only listener. It is not a public deployment option.
Do not relax peer restrictions to work around a reachability problem.

TLS requires `--features tls`, an explicit listener and operator-provided
PEM certificate/key files. Use a certificate trusted by the intended
clients. There is no automatic renewal or file reload; replacement needs
an operator-managed restart, which loses active state. Local browser tests
bypass trust for their generated certificate and do not qualify public PKI.

TLS protects client-to-relay transport. It does not turn arbitrary forwarded
payloads into end-to-end encrypted media; the endpoint protocol owns that.

## Lifecycle and observability

The CLI runs in the foreground and emits startup/errors to stderr. It has
no daemonisation, HTTP health endpoint, admin UI, per-client access log or
recording feature. An embedding host can read aggregate `Server::stats()`
and `allocation_count()`; no remote metrics exporter is included.

Use the operator's process supervision and restrictive environment/file
permissions. Stop a local instance with Ctrl-C. Restart closes existing
allocations; graceful drain and live configuration reload are not present.
See [security](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/SECURITY.md), [qualification](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/GOALS.md) and the
[transport position](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/legal/transport-position.md) for the remaining boundaries.

---

## Source: Security

Canonical source: [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/SECURITY.md)

# Security policy

spry-turn 0.1.0 is an initial implementation. It has local socket/browser
verification and bounded parsing/state, but no independent security audit
or production qualification. See [verification](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/verification.md) and
[remaining work](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/GOALS.md).

## Report a vulnerability

The repository is private and no public security inbox is promised. Ask a
maintainer for an agreed private reporting channel using a minimal
access-controlled issue. Do not include an exploit, credential, production
endpoint, private media or personal information in that initial request.
Share the detailed report only through the channel the maintainer confirms.
No response-time guarantee is offered.

For an ordinary synthetic bug report, see [support](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/SUPPORT.md).

## Boundaries

- The shared TURN secret belongs only to an operator's trusted server or
  credential tool; short-lived usernames/passwords go to clients.
- Nonces, integrity checks, peer policy, allocation expiry and resource
  limits protect transport state. They do not enforce room membership.
- Client TLS ends at the relay. Payload confidentiality depends on the
  endpoint protocol; arbitrary TURN traffic is not automatically opaque.
- Loopback peers require explicit local-test configuration. Do not expose
  a relaxed private-address proxy to untrusted clients.
- The default connected-UDP optimisation costs an extra socket per UDP
  allocation. Bound process descriptors as well as logical allocations.
- WASM framing does not provide network I/O, allocation authorisation or
  permission checks for a host-supplied adapter.

Do not assume unsupported coturn extensions or operational controls exist.
Use [the compatibility map](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/coturn-compatibility.md) before evaluation.

## Source: Native M4 benchmarks

Canonical source: [docs/benchmarks.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md)

# Measured comparison

23 October 2026. The final, architecture-matched Apple M4 Max run shows
17–22% higher delivered-packet throughput than the coturn configuration
tested, about 19–23% less server CPU time for the complete workload, and
78–82% less process RSS. These are UDP loopback measurements, not a claim
about maximum WAN capacity, TLS performance or every coturn configuration.

## Final native ARM64 results

Medians of three runs per row. Both servers and the shared Rust load
generator were thin ARM64 executables. Each throughput run completed
200,000 round trips, counting 400,000 successfully forwarded data packets.
All 36 runs completed: 14.4 million forwarded packets with no observed
loss, reordering or corruption. Units below are decimal kB/MB/Gbit/s.

| Payload | Allocations | spry-turn packets/s | coturn packets/s | spry throughput gain | spry RSS MB | coturn RSS MB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 160 B | 1 | 274,471 | 224,479 | 22.3% | 1.72 | 7.96 |
| 160 B | 16 | 293,864 | 250,261 | 17.4% | 1.82 | 8.39 |
| 160 B | 128 | 302,206 | 252,816 | 19.5% | 2.03 | 11.42 |
| 1,200 B | 1 | 263,649 | 216,849 | 21.6% | 1.72 | 7.96 |
| 1,200 B | 16 | 282,584 | 242,327 | 16.6% | 1.82 | 8.45 |
| 1,200 B | 128 | 292,124 | 245,148 | 19.2% | 2.06 | 11.37 |

At 128 allocations and 1,200-byte payloads, aggregate forwarded payload
rate is 2.804 Gbit/s against 2.353 Gbit/s. Complete-run server CPU is
1.436 s against 1.797 s. That CPU accounting includes startup, allocation
setup, warm-up and the separate latency samples, not just the timed data
loop. It excludes the separate load-generator process.

| Payload | Allocations | spry RTT p50 / p99 µs | coturn RTT p50 / p99 µs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 160 B | 1 | 39.7 / 173.8 | 36.0 / 258.7 |
| 160 B | 16 | 38.0 / 178.0 | 39.5 / 223.0 |
| 160 B | 128 | 37.2 / 48.2 | 39.3 / 48.3 |
| 1,200 B | 1 | 31.4 / 249.7 | 38.3 / 250.7 |
| 1,200 B | 16 | 38.8 / 229.8 | 41.3 / 224.4 |
| 1,200 B | 128 | 38.9 / 48.5 | 40.4 / 50.5 |

These are medians of per-run percentiles from 2,000 single-round-trip
samples taken before each throughput phase. Round trips include the client,
both relay directions and the echo peer; they are not isolated server
processing latency. Lower-load tail latency is visibly affected by host
scheduling. There is no claim of a latency improvement in every row.

## What changed

The server reserves space before received peer payloads and writes TURN
headers there, avoiding a second media-payload copy. Internal readiness
tokens use bounded, generation-tagged slots instead of hash lookups; stale
events cannot address a newly allocated client in a reused slot.

The main measured gain came from connected client-facing UDP sockets for
authenticated, concrete-IPv4 allocations. They preserve the original TURN
five-tuple and use connected send/receive while retaining normal allocation,
authentication and peer-permission rules. Wildcard/IPv6 listeners and failed
socket optimisations use the standard path. A separate faster-hash
experiment gave little benefit and its dependency was removed.

The [matched three-way experiment](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/m4-native-connected.json)
compared the portable native baseline, the connected variant and coturn in
alternating order. At 128 allocations/1,200 B their median rates were
246,541, 292,350 and 246,694 packets/s respectively. It supports attributing
the gain to the implementation change, rather than to changing architecture.

There is a resource trade-off. At 128 UDP allocations, the optimised server
holds **257 UDP sockets**, against **129** in the baseline and coturn.
Process RSS excludes kernel socket buffers and other kernel memory. Total
system memory for those sockets was not measured. File-descriptor budgets
must therefore account for two UDP sockets per optimised allocation, plus
listeners and any TCP/TLS connections.

## Method and limits

- Apple M4 Max, 16 logical CPUs, macOS 26.6.2 / Darwin 25.6.0. Existing host
  workloads were left running. Final-run load averages and every raw sample
  are recorded, not a claim of an otherwise empty machine.
- Rust 1.96, explicit `aarch64-apple-darwin` target, release optimisation,
  LTO, one codegen unit, aborting panics and stripped symbols. Generic ARM64
  target; no M4-only instruction tuning or profile-guided optimisation.
- Unmodified coturn 4.18.0 source, SHA-256 pinned by the preparation script,
  `-O3 -DNDEBUG`, database backends and Prometheus disabled, libevent 2.1.13
  and OpenSSL 3.6.4. One relay event loop (`relay-threads=0`); no TLS/DTLS,
  TCP relay allocations or administration in the measured workload.
- Same REST shared-secret authentication, allocation/user limits and
  1 GiB/s per-allocation bandwidth ceiling for both. The elevated ceiling
  avoids benchmarking the default bandwidth limiter. Both explicitly allow
  loopback peers only for these tests.
- Shared native Rust generator, 32 round trips in flight per worker; one
  load worker for one allocation, four for 16/128, rotating across their
  allocations. It checks sequence numbers, peer source and every returned
  payload byte. This closed-loop workload does not establish maximum server
  capacity or simulate 128 continuously saturated independent clients.
- Alternating server order, fresh processes and credentials for each run,
  4,096 process descriptor limit applied equally. RSS sampled every 50 ms;
  very short peaks can be missed. No off-machine test traffic.
- TLS is tested functionally by independent sockets and generated browser
  media; it is not included in these throughput figures. Long-duration,
  lossy-network, Linux, real-phone and Archy acceptance remain separate work.

The UDP/TCP executable is **402,912 bytes**. The measured coturn reference
is 487,032 bytes after `strip -x`; removing its remaining symbol information
gives 462,616 bytes. These executable sizes exclude coturn's required shared
libraries. The optional TLS build and WASM codec are separate artefacts;
the WASM framing test measures no network forwarding.

The first run series mistakenly used an x86_64 Rust executable and generator
under Rosetta against native coturn. Those figures are explicitly
superseded, retained in `evidence/m4-results*.json` for traceability, and are
not used above. A separate earlier attempt hit the generator's inherited
256-descriptor limit. The runner now records binary architectures, refuses
a mismatch when `--required-arch` is set, and sets the descriptor limit.

## Reproduce

Build on the machine being measured; choose the explicit native target.
The preparation script builds its reference and any missing pkg-config
helper inside the supplied scratch directory without installing a service.

```sh
cargo build --locked --release --target aarch64-apple-darwin \
  --bin spry-turn --example load
python3 scripts/prepare-coturn.py .local/reference
python3 scripts/compare.py \
  --spry target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/spry-turn \
  --loader target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/examples/load \
  --coturn .local/reference/coturn-4.18.0/bin/turnserver \
  --required-arch arm64 --runs 3 --clients 1 16 128 --sizes 160 1200 \
  --packets 200000 --output .local/m4-results.json
```

Raw [final results](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/m4-native-final.json),
[native baseline](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/m4-native-baseline.json),
[controlled tuning experiment](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/m4-native-connected.json),
[build receipt](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/m4-build.json) and
[reviewed source manifest](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/source-manifest.json) are the evidence.
No credentials, real endpoints, machine paths or media are included.

## Source: Verification

Canonical source: [docs/verification.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/verification.md)

# Standalone verification

## Bounded relay ports, local increment

The optional UDP relay-port range passed 22 independent socket tests with
the default TLS build, including a signed 508 on exhaustion, occupied-port
skipping, reuse after deallocation and continued forwarding by another
allocation. Chromium passed relay-only generated audio/video/data over
UDP, TCP and TLS, with selected local and remote relay ports asserted
inside the configured range. See the [bounded receipt](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/bounded-relay-ports-20261023.json).
The existing initial-release benchmark and hosted CI below do not qualify
this new runtime change. Public firewall/NAT, certificate lifecycle, Archy
installation and phone acceptance remain unverified.

## Initial implementation evidence

23 October 2026. Private MIT software project; no public relay, credential
endpoint, application service or Archy integration has been deployed.

- Rust fmt and all-feature clippy passed with warnings denied.
- Eight all-feature unit tests passed, including the published STUN vector,
  tampering, parsing bounds, nonce binding/expiry, rate accounting, private
  peer policy and stale-event isolation with bounded slot reuse.
- Minimal builds passed: one limits test without features; six codec/auth
  tests without the socket runtime.
- All 19 independent socket tests passed with the TLS build, including UDP,
  TCP, TLS, framing, credentials, quotas, expiry, permissions, indications,
  channel traffic and isolation across deallocation/reallocation.
- Chromium passed relay-only data round trips, decoded generated video and
  received audio at both endpoints over UDP, TCP and TLS. No real camera,
  microphone recording or production room was used. Browser TLS tests use
  explicit test-certificate bypass; the independent Python TLS client
  validates the generated certificate through its test CA.
- Actual WASM execution validated the STUN integrity vector and a million
  arena framing/parsing operations without linear-memory growth. Its timing
  is a protocol microbenchmark, not a network performance measurement.
- The final native ARM64 M4 comparison completed all 36 runs, 14.4 million
  forwarded packets, with no observed data loss, reordering or corruption.
  See [method, trade-offs and raw evidence](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md).
- The staged source/credential scan passed without an ignore rule. Recorded
  checksum fields use explicit path/SHA-256 records; no test credentials,
  private endpoints, machine paths or actual media are committed.

GitHub hosting is private under `forgesworn/spry-turn`; publication to package
registries, image registries, public releases and Pages remains disabled or
absent. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/actions/runs/40015270709)
passed on Linux and macOS for implementation commit
`48d75adf51c73b1ef2a51a3cb663e424f2b4ea35`. That run predates the bounded-port
increment; hosted CI is separate evidence from the new local checks.

Retained local build evidence is ignored by Git:

- `.local/bin/spry-turn`: tested native executable with optional TLS enabled.
- `.local/wasm/`: generated WASM module and JavaScript/TypeScript bindings.
- `.local/evidence/m4-benchmark-source.tar.gz`: exact M4 benchmark source
  snapshot, identified by the committed build receipt. Rustfmt normalisation
  matches the reviewed Rust files. Repository ownership metadata subsequently
  changed to the ForgeSworn organisation without changing runtime source.

Task-owned test servers and browsers have stopped. The M4 scratch tree was
removed after evidence capture, and `cargo clean` removed 340.2 MiB of local
build output. Existing unrelated host services are preserved. Real-phone,
lossy-network, Linux performance, full coturn conformance and public operator
acceptance remain the explicit later gates in [GOALS.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/GOALS.md).

## Source: Acceptance and roadmap

Canonical source: [GOALS.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/GOALS.md)

# Compatibility and acceptance

## First standalone implementation

- [x] Original Rust STUN/TURN parser with published integrity test vector.
- [x] Real UDP allocations and bidirectional relaying.
- [x] Coturn-compatible shared-secret REST credentials, signed responses,
  stateless address-bound nonces and expiry.
- [x] UDP, TCP and optional TLS client transports, with bounded stream buffers.
- [x] Permissions, ChannelBind, indications, refresh/delete and allocation retry.
- [x] Local Chromium relay-only data and decoded media over UDP/TCP/TLS.
- [x] M4 comparison against unmodified coturn, with method and raw results.
- [x] Native connected-UDP and direct-readiness-slot tuning, tested against
  a native baseline and coturn with resource costs recorded.
- [x] WASM protocol arena, actual execution and bounded buffer reuse test.
- [x] Private repository, source/secret review and CI readback.

## Before replacing an existing deployment

- [x] Operator-selected bounded UDP relay port range and firewall/certificate plan.
- [ ] Applied firewall/NAT, trusted public certificate lifecycle and independent
  cross-network deployment acceptance; a local plan is not this evidence.
- [ ] Real KithMoot web and native interoperability against a separately chosen
  server, without adding a project-operated credential service.
- [ ] Packet-loss, jitter, blocked UDP, IPv6, long-lived refresh, reconnect,
  certificate validation/renewal and resource-exhaustion qualification.
- [ ] Broader RFC conformance suite and sustained coverage-guided fuzzing.
- [ ] Independent security review, including nonce/auth state and relay targets.
- [ ] Static long-term user credentials if the target deployments require them.
- [ ] Decide whether supported coturn deployments need EVEN-PORT, reservation
  tokens, dual allocations, RFC 8489 SHA-256 auth or other extensions.
  Unsupported comprehension-required attributes currently receive 420.
- [ ] Measure Linux batching and multiple independent workers before adding
  platform-specific fast paths. macOS results cannot prove Linux performance.

TCP relay allocations (RFC 6062), DTLS client transport, database integrations,
OAuth, telnet/HTTP administration and clustering are outside the first release.
TURN over TCP/TLS still uses UDP sockets between the relay and its peers.
Do not silently remove transport support required by existing clients.

## Later integrations

- [ ] Archy operator-owned package, identity-independent transport credentials,
  deliberate opt-in exposure and resource limits. No default hosted service.
- [ ] Swift/Kotlin boundary and physical no-Play GrapheneOS acceptance if a
  native app needs to host a relay, separately from ordinary TURN client use.
- [ ] Assess Sapflow transport needs without adding codecs, SRT or HLS to the
  forwarding core, or claiming unmodified clients already speak TURN.

# Changelog

## Unreleased

- Optional inclusive `--relay-ports FIRST:LAST` bounds UDP peer allocations.
  Occupied ports are skipped; exhaustion returns 508 without falling back
  outside the range. Existing default ephemeral allocation is unchanged.
- Operator firewall/NAT/certificate plan and bounded-range socket/browser
  regression coverage. Public deployment qualification remains open.

## 0.1.0 — 23 October 2026

Initial private prerelease. No package registry, public relay or Archy
deployment is included. Full coturn parity and production qualification
remain open.

- Standalone Rust server and embeddable native library with STUN Binding,
  authenticated TURN UDP allocations, permissions, ChannelData and indications.
- UDP/TCP clients, optional rustls TLS, expiring shared-secret credentials
  and bounded allocation, connection and bandwidth resources.
- Borrowed forwarding buffers, generation-tagged readiness slots and the
  concrete-IPv4 connected-UDP optimisation, with socket trade-offs disclosed.
- Native ARM64 M4 Max comparison against coturn 4.18.0, with complete raw
  results and superseded translated-architecture runs identified.
- WASM packet arena and credential helpers, verified through actual execution.
- Independent UDP/TCP/TLS socket checks, relay-only generated browser media,
  Linux/macOS CI and explicit remaining qualification gates.
- Installation, integration, API, operations and coturn compatibility guides;
  ForgeSworn donation links and generated LLM navigation/full context checked
  for freshness in CI.

## Source: Contributing

Canonical source: [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

# Contributing

Read [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/AGENTS.md) and [GOALS.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/GOALS.md). Keep the forwarding core
small, safe Rust and independent of media, application admission and hosted
services. Keep the repository, prerelease and fixtures private unless the
owner explicitly authorises public publication.

Use synthetic peers, credentials and media. Do not commit private endpoints,
real machine paths, keys or packet captures. Use this checkout's `target/`
and leave `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` unchanged.

## Documentation

```sh
npm run docs:generate
npm run check:docs
```

These commands use Node 24 built-ins, without `npm install`. Edit source
guides rather than generated `llms.txt` or `llms-full.txt`. The checker
validates generated context, local links, heading anchors and funding
destinations. See [maintaining documentation](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/maintaining-docs.md).

## Native checks

```sh
npm run check
cargo build --locked --release --features tls
python3 tests/interop.py --tls
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npx playwright install chromium
python3 tests/browser.py --tls
```

`npm run check` runs documentation validation, Rust formatting, clippy with
warnings denied, all-feature tests and both minimal library test sets.
Python orchestrates independent test sockets and browser fixtures; the
shipping server, library and socket load generator are Rust.

For WASM build and actual execution, use [the API commands](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/api.md#wasm-build).
Run an appropriate credential/source scan before pushing; never suppress a
finding without inspecting and resolving its cause. Current CI runs native
checks and interop on Linux/macOS and builds the WASM codec on Linux.

## Performance and cleanup

Performance claims require matched executable architectures, real socket
workloads, alternating server order and disclosed resource costs. Use
[the existing benchmark method](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md); a framing microbenchmark
cannot establish network throughput. Preserve raw failure evidence alongside
successful runs and do not confuse loopback with production acceptance.

Stop task-owned servers and browsers and remove their fixtures. After a
safe merge, remove only build/scratch resources created by that task.
Preserve the explicitly named benchmark and verification evidence.

## Source: Coding-agent instructions

Canonical source: [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/AGENTS.md)

# spry-turn

A small packet relay. Keep protocol adapters separate from forwarding and
resource limits. WebRTC, SRT, media codecs and media packaging are not runtime
dependencies. Transparent UDP is for an explicitly configured upstream;
TURN is optional. Do not silently turn either into an open arbitrary proxy.

- British English. MIT. Commit as TheCryptoDonkey with a GitHub no-reply email.
- This repository starts private. Do not publish packages, images, releases,
  pages or public repositories without the owner's instruction.
- No real endpoints, credentials, private source, media or machine paths in
  committed evidence. Fixtures must be generated locally.
- `unsafe` is forbidden in our code. Keep dependency features small.
- Use this checkout's `target/`. Leave `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` unchanged.
- Test outside-input parsing, authentication, permissions, state expiry and
  overload. Performance claims require reproducible socket measurements.
- Run fmt, clippy, tests, minimal-feature builds, interop and secret scanning.
- Stop task-owned servers and remove generated private fixtures afterwards.

## Source: Maintaining documentation

Canonical source: [docs/maintaining-docs.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/maintaining-docs.md)

# Maintaining documentation and discovery

Maintained source lives in the Markdown guides linked from
[the documentation index](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/README.md). `scripts/docs.mjs` owns the catalogue,
generates both LLM files and checks all tracked Markdown/TXT navigation.
The generator uses Node built-ins; it adds no server runtime dependency.

## Edit, generate, check

1. Update the relevant source guide and any changed examples or limitations.
2. Add a new primary guide to the catalogue in `scripts/docs.mjs` and the
   documentation index.
3. Run `npm run docs:generate`, then `npm run check:docs`.
4. Commit source and generated files together. CI rejects stale output,
   missing local files, broken local heading fragments and mismatched
   donation destinations.

`llms.txt` is a concise Markdown navigation file following
[the llms.txt proposal](https://llmstxt.org/). `llms-full.txt` bundles the
maintained guides using canonical absolute GitHub links. Both carry the
version and important implementation/qualification boundaries. Raw benchmark
JSON, dependency licence dumps, machine paths and ignored fixtures are not
bundled. Generated links use the canonical `forgesworn/spry-turn` repository.

The checker is deterministic and offline. It validates repository links
and fragments, not external site availability or GitHub rendering of a
Sponsor button. Recheck external donation pages when changing recipients.

## Repository metadata and privacy

Keep the GitHub description, repository topics, Cargo description, keywords
and documentation URL accurate. `publish = false` and npm's `private: true`
continue to block package publication. The private repository's root
`llms.txt` helps authorised tools; unauthenticated crawlers cannot read it.
There is no claim of search-engine ranking, model training inclusion or
guaranteed ingestion.

If public publication is authorised later, independently review source,
history, fixtures, release artefacts and legal position before changing
visibility. Do not add a public Pages site or copy private documentation to
a public domain just to improve discovery. Donation links are informational
and never grant transport or application access.

## Ship checklist

Run [the required checks](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), inspect the staged diff and
scan for secrets. Push a branch, merge its reviewed PR only after Linux/macOS
CI succeeds, then verify the merged head. Tag the reviewed commit and make
the GitHub release a private prerelease. Verify the tag target, release
visibility and any downloaded asset checksums. Public packages, images,
Pages and a running TURN service require their own explicit scope.

Release builds must remap the builder's home-directory prefix before
packaging, so panic/source strings do not disclose private machine paths.
For example, supply `RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=$HOME=/build"` to each
native and WASM release build. Scan the resulting binaries as well as
source. Include the MIT licence, dependency notices and a platform/scope
README in archives; publish SHA-256 checksums and a source-commit receipt.

## Source: Transport position

Canonical source: [docs/legal/transport-position.md](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/legal/transport-position.md)

# Packet transport position

Draft, 23 October 2026. Not legal advice; not reviewed by a lawyer. This is
a design position for the local implementation, not a deployment or
compliance assessment. The reviewed source is identified by file hashes in
the [source manifest](https://github.com/forgesworn/spry-turn/blob/main/docs/evidence/source-manifest.json).

The legal source is jurisdiction-kit's [GB online-services
note](https://github.com/forgesworn/jurisdiction-kit/blob/main/law/gb/online-services.md),
verified overall on 28 September 2026 and due for review by 28 March 2027.
The local note includes partial primary-source checks dated 23 October
2026 for transport access facilities, public communications providers and
investigatory powers; those additions may precede the linked public copy.
`[P]` means primary text read in that note, not a settled application.
`[U]` means an unresolved interpretation or application to this design.

## Position today and intended operation

The owner has chosen software publication without a maintainer-operated
default relay or central KithMoot calling entitlement. The repository starts
private, under MIT, with package publication disabled (`Cargo.toml:6`, `:14`).
The owner reports local implementation and tests only: no service is
deployed. Code publication, a build and a running communications service
are separate events. No public operational service is established by the
presence of server source.

The intended deployment is a standalone, coturn-style TURN server on an
independently operated Archy node. KithMoot would select it through ordinary
TURN configuration. Integration, actual operator independence and device
acceptance remain unproved. Sapflow support is a later optional goal.
Nothing here changes another application's deployment or legal position.

## Implemented boundary

The library's default listener is loopback; the executable requires an
operator-provided secret and explicit configuration to expose another
address (`src/turn.rs:127`, `src/main.rs:54`, `:82`). There is no runtime
hosted endpoint default or discovery lookup. The source has no application
room model, member directory, room-invitation authority or KithMoot
entitlement issuer. TURN resource authentication is separate from admission
to an application conversation. The REST credential
helper accepts an operator secret and a username, while server nonces bind
to address, time and realm (`src/auth.rs:13`, `:29`, `:54`, `:73`). An operator
that holds the secret can issue transport credentials; that fact does not give
it room membership authority (`src/turn.rs:868`).

Allocation, permission, channel and connection state is held in memory,
with expiry and capacity limits (`src/turn.rs:213`, `:351`, `:798`, `:1065`,
`:1114`, `:1295`, `:1348`). The forwarding paths relay datagrams between sockets
and keep aggregate packet/byte/drop counters (`src/turn.rs:908`, `:1358`,
`:1392`; `src/limits.rs:41`). The default optimisation can add a connected
client-facing UDP socket per authenticated UDP allocation for a concrete IPv4
listener on Unix, with a portable fallback (`Cargo.toml:17`, `:23`;
`src/turn.rs:395`, `:1103`). This retains the same transport credentials,
permissions and application-admission boundary. The reviewed code has no
payload-recording or per-client access-log writer. It emits startup/error diagnostics, and the
credential subcommand deliberately prints a credential pair
(`src/main.rs:36`, `:119`, `:152`). Host logs, shell history, process
inspection, crash handling and any service wrapper require a separate
deployment audit; in-memory expiry is not a forensic-erasure claim.

The relay handles network addresses, credential identifiers, permissions,
connection state and forwarded datagram bytes. It is not an end-to-end
media encryption implementation. Payload confidentiality depends on the
endpoints and application protocol. TLS terminates at the relay, which can
inspect the forwarded bytes after that link's protection is removed.
Use opaque transport-only credential labels: do not encode room identities
or personal identifiers merely for relay authentication.

## Legal reasoning and change boundary

The note's sections 1 and 2.2 distinguish software publication from service
operation. For the intended independent node, OSA section 226(12)'s
access-facility distinction exists `[P]` (note 2.11). Applying it to this
TURN deployment, separately from the underlying call service and its
admission authority, remains `[U]`. Replaceable, room-blind transport and
real independence support that distinction; encryption, a separate process
or a licence alone do not establish an exemption. Ordinary room invitations
are not automatically operation of the underlying service `[U]` (note 2.2).

A running node's metadata processing and any public forwarding need their
own conditional data-protection, communications and lawful-notice assessment
(note sections 3, 4.1, 5 and 7); this publisher position does not settle those
roles or promise immunity from legal process.

Before adopting the Archy deployment, confirm its actual operator,
credential control, independent substitution and separation from room
admission. Adding maintainer-run defaults, compulsory calling entitlements,
room control, discovery or media processing requires a fresh assessment.
Do not silently make ordinary client installations transit nodes. No
service-launch deadline or fee is assigned by this local publisher-only
assessment.

Not checked: non-UK law; actual Archy/KithMoot/Sapflow integration; live
infrastructure; real-device acceptance; or a complete public relay operator
assessment.
